references.text: Laban confronts Jacob about the stolen teraphim, and Rachel succeeds in hiding them from her father.
Jacob asks his family and all who are with him to remove foreign gods among them, indicating that the household had idols, including the teraphim Rachel stole from Laban.
Mica made an ephod and teraphim (household gods), showing that teraphim were widespread in Israel as a form of idolatry.
Michal uses a household god image (teraphim) to deceive Saul's messengers, illustrating another event where teraphim play a role in a deceptive act.
Hosea prophesies that the children of Israel will sit many days without teraphim and other religious objects, highlighting the role of teraphim in Israel's religious practice.
The candidate continues the same sequence of events directly after the theft and shows the consequences of the action.
Creating narrative tension by showing Jacob's uncertainty about Rachel's actions within the same event sequence.
